reasoning: Failure-driven edits (Group 1) are kept in full because they fix fatal format and selection errors: tool-name formatting, bracket separators, bare-name parameters, the required/optional split, locale values, one-call-per-clause, named checks, and every listed retailer. Group 2's two success edits cover patterns the failure edits do not: matching endpoints by description echo, and copying values verbatim in the schema's form. They do not conflict with any failure edit and target separate text regions, so both are kept. All targets exist in the current skill, none touch the protected SLOW_UPDATE section, and no edits duplicate each other, so no deduplication was needed.

edits.target: Never give only the provider or only the endpoint, even when the query names the tool loosely.
edits.content: Never give only the provider or only the endpoint, even when the query names the tool loosely. The name is ONLY the `### ` heading line, joined as `Provider: API` (colon + space). The `Provider: X — tagline` line under it is a description, not a name: never include ` — `, ` - `, any tagline text, or a dash between provider and API, and never repeat the name twice (wrong: `Wayfair — auto-complete`, `Wayfair — products/get-images`, `Rocket League: News — Rocket League: News`, `Hearthstone — This API provides cards...: Get Cards`; right: `Wayfair: auto-complete`, `Wayfair: products/get-images`, `Rocket League: News`, `Hearthstone: Get Cards`). Nothing follows the endpoint name.

edits.target: Do not close the list early or leave stray brackets.
edits.content: Do not close the list early or leave stray brackets. Calls are separated only by `}, {`. Never write `}],{`, `], [` or `]]` between or after calls. A single `]` follows the last object, immediately before `</answer>`. This holds for long answers of 9 or more calls too.

'US English' -> `en-US` only when the schema lists `en-US` (otherwise `en`). Use only values the schema lists; never invent a locale such as `en-US` when the list shows `en`. A nationality or place word ('US technology headlines') -> category `technology`, country `us`, language `en` when the tool has those fields. 'Helpful reviews' -> sort_order `HELPFUL`.

edits.target: - Each parameter is `{"name": "x", "value": "y"}`. Every value is a quoted string, including numbers (`"2023"`, `"1"`, `"9098084"`).
edits.content: - Both lists hold ONLY `{"name","value"}` objects with a real value taken from the query. Never write bare names (wrong: `"required parameters": ["page"]`; right: `[{"name": "page", "value": "1"}]`). A required parameter always gets the query's value (region `us`, version `v1`, location `global`, page `1`). Copy the schema's split exactly: only names listed under 'Required parameters' go in `required parameters`. If the schema says `Required parameters: none`, that list is `[]` and every value (airports, flight number, carrier, date, ...) goes in `optional parameters`. If a schema lists `sku` as required and `postalCode` as optional, `postalCode` stays optional. Every object keeps all three keys, e.g. `"optional parameters": []` even when empty.

edits.target: - Do not add 'helper', 'random', 'new releases' or 'list' calls that no clause names.
edits.content:
- A list of items ('US tech headlines, general global news, Arabic news from BBC, anime updates') means one call per item, each with its own endpoint. Do not let one headlines tool absorb two items. 'General/global/latest news' -> the broad recent-news endpoint (e.g. `Moka News: Recent 50`), separate from the topic-specific headlines call. 'Check if Asos carries similar products' -> Asos's product search/auto-complete endpoint with q set to the product (e.g. `modern sectional sofa`), not `categories/list`.
- One clause = one call. Never emit the same tool twice with alternative parameters to 'cover both readings' (e.g. one schedules call with DepartureDateTime and another with ArrivalDateTime; 'flight from SFO on May 25' = one call with DepartureDateTime plus the airports, carrier and flight number as optionals). Repeat a call only when the query asks for the action twice.
- N named checks = N calls, one tool each, each tool's description matching its check. 'Existence, MX records and deliverability' = the verify tool, the MX tool, and the tool whose description says deliverable/valid. Do not add format-only or disposable checkers the query does not name.
- Every retailer or platform the query lists ('BestBuy, Wayfair, Zappos, and Aliexpress') gets its own search call with the product term, even when later clauses give SKUs or IDs for some of them. Check each listed name before answering.

- Fill every field the clause implies. A locale ('US region with USD currency') on a tool with `store`, `country`, `currency`, `sizeSchema`, `lang` fills all of them that the locale determines (store `US`, country `US`, currency `USD`, sizeSchema `US`, lang `en-US` only if the schema lists it). A count ('find 5 puzzles') goes in the count field (`count` `5`). Several values for one field ('endgame and promotion themes') go in that one parameter in the schema's list style (e.g. `["endgame","promotion"]`), plus any match-mode field (themesType `ALL` for 'and'). Scope words ('global stats', 'US region') are values themselves (`global`, `us`), matching the case of the schema's examples. A US state for a state parameter -> the 2-letter code (`WA`) unless the schema shows full names.

edits.content: - Match each clause to the endpoint whose description echoes the clause's own words, numbers or noun, and skip generic siblings. Examples: 'price change of 5% or more in a day' -> the small-cap-gainers endpoint; 'revenue and earnings growth exceeding 25%' -> the growth-technology-stocks endpoint; 'mathematical facts' -> the math-fact endpoint and 'trivia fact' -> the trivia-fact endpoint (two numbers, two calls); 'scrape email addresses from a website' -> the scraper endpoint; 'historical volatility' -> the volatility endpoint, not a technical-indicator endpoint.

edits.target: Never emit a parameter with an empty value.
edits.content: - Copy values verbatim from the query as strings: IDs, keys, codes (keep leading zeros, `026000`), URLs and timestamps (`1659312000000`). Give each value in the form the schema asks for. If the parameter is `email`, pass the full address even when the clause says 'MX records for this email domain'. If the parameter is `domain`, pass the bare domain (`premiumwidgets.co`). A lone identifier in a clause goes to that tool's id-like parameter (`video_id`, `key`, `drill_id`, `kode_wilayah_kabupaten_id`). Explicit start and end values map to the tool's matching start/end fields even when they are optional.
